---
title: "Ethical dilemma: AI recruitment and gender discrimination at Amazon"
author: Molly Liao
date: November 25, 2026
---

In 2018, Reuters reported that Amazon developed an experimental AI recruitment tool to automate resume screening. The system was trained using resumes submitted to Amazon over a ten-year period and attempted to rank applicants from one to five stars. However, because most of the resumes came from men, the algorithm learned patterns that favoured male applicants; it penalized resumes containing the word "women's" and downgraded graduates from two women's colleges. Although Amazon attempted to correct these biases, it could not guarantee that the algorithm would not discriminate in other ways. The company eventually abandoned the project.

The ethical dilemma What concerns me about this example is that AI is increasingly being used everywhere, including as a filter between applicants and recruiters. As an international student, visa-sponsership is something we have to consider when applying for jobs, and I am concerned that the AI has been applied to mark-down or even filter out applications for those who need sponsership. The dilemma the use of algorithm and large data and AI is I have to consider whether a company is willing to sponsor my visa when applying for internships/ jobs. I wonder if an AI system saw the words "visa sponsorship" in my application and interpreted them negatively. Even if I have the qualifications for a position, I could potentially be filtered out before a human recruiter has the opportunity to review my application. This makes me question whether AI recruitment actually makes hiring more objective or simply makes existing biases less visible.
